definitions: ["a cylinder on which film, wire, thread, or other flexible materials can be wound"]
examples: ["the wires may be rolled on to a simple reel", "the projectionist changed reels", "a cotton reel"]

definitions: ["a length of something wound on to a reel"]
["a device for winding and unwinding a line as required, in particular the line attached to a fishing rod"]
["a part or section of a film (originally the amount that could fit on one reel of film)"]
examples: ["in the final reel he is transformed from unhinged sociopath into local hero"]

definitions: ["a collection of short videos or film clips, especially as shown on social media"]
examples: ["the reel featured a compilation of her videos and pictures", "those goals are on the highlights reel for a reason", "Mira shared an Instagram reel that features herself"]

definitions: ["a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance"]
examples: ["we put on the record player and danced reels", "an eightsome reel"]

definitions: ["a piece of music for a reel, typically in simple or duple time"]
["wind something on to a reel by turning the reel"]
examples: ["sailplanes are often launched by means of a wire reeled in by a winch"]

definitions: ["bring in a fish attached to a line by turning a reel and winding in the line"]
examples: ["he reeled in a good perch", "he struck, and reeled in a good perch"]

definitions: ["lose one's balance and stagger or lurch violently"]
examples: ["he punched Connolly in the ear, sending him reeling", "Cormack reeled as the ship began to roll", "she reeled back against the van"]

definitions: ["walk in a staggering or lurching manner, especially while drunk"]
examples: ["the two reeled out of the bar arm in arm"]

definitions: ["feel shocked, bewildered, or giddy"]
examples: ["we are reeling from the response we've had", "the alcohol made my head reel", "the unaccustomed intake of alcohol made my head reel"]

definitions: ["dance a reel"]
